title: 大学 ESL 学术英语写作与同行评审 AI 评估
question: In undergraduate ESL/EAP academic English writing courses, does allowing students to use generative AI writing and peer-review assistants improve argumentative essay quality and critical thinking, and what are the over-reliance and originality risks?

nodes.name: ev-esl-01: Thesis-Evidence Coherence & Move Structure (g=+0.58)
nodes.quote: Structured Socratic outline prompts significantly improved Toulmin argument structure and claim-evidence alignment in first-draft essays (g=+0.58).

nodes.name: ev-esl-02: Academic Vocabulary Density & Collocation Sophistication (g=+0.48)
nodes.quote: Contextual academic synonym suggestions elevated AWL vocabulary density by 28% without increasing lexical distortion (g=+0.48).

nodes.name: ev-esl-03: Unassisted Delayed Essay Reasoning Score (g=-0.24)
nodes.quote: Unguarded access to auto-generated paragraphs degraded independent counter-argument construction on unassisted exams (g=-0.24).

nodes.name: ev-esl-04: Authorial Voice Strength & Agency Rubric (g=+0.42)
nodes.quote: Mandatory reflection logs requiring students to justify accepting/rejecting AI revisions preserved individual authorial stance (g=+0.42).

nodes.name: ev-esl-05: Global Revision Uptake & Argument Validity (g=+0.52)
nodes.quote: Combining AI mechanical diagnostics with peer evaluative critique yielded higher revision quality than peer-only or AI-only arms (g=+0.52).

nodes.name: ev-esl-06: CARS Move Sequence Accuracy (g=+0.61)
nodes.quote: Formative AI move feedback accelerated mastery of Swales CARS introductory framework (g=+0.61).

nodes.name: ev-esl-07: Coh-Metrix Connective Indices & Lexical Sophistication (g=+0.45)
nodes.quote: Interactive cohesive device prompts improved global text connectivity and Academic Formulas List usage (g=+0.45).

nodes.name: ev-esl-08: Delayed Solo Essay Counter-Argument Depth (g=-0.28)
nodes.quote: Students writing with continuous AI sentence generation showed a 28% drop in solo rebuttals during a 4-week delayed assessment (g=-0.28).

nodes.name: ev-esl-09: Cross-Student Lexical Entropy & Idiolect Uniqueness (g=-0.20)
nodes.quote: Unconstrained sentence rewriting caused stylistic homogenization across student cohorts, suppressing distinctive rhetoric (g=-0.20).

nodes.name: ev-esl-10: Global Writing Quality Composite (g=+0.51)
nodes.quote: Synthesis across 34 empirical trials demonstrates consistent in-task structural gains when AI feedback is scaffolded (g=+0.51).

nodes.name: ev-esl-11: Paraphrase Originality & Citation Traceability (g=+0.39)
nodes.quote: Prompting students to verify AI source syntheses against primary literature significantly reduced patchwriting (g=+0.39).

nodes.name: ev-esl-12: Argument Fallacy Identification & Rebuttal Strength (g=+0.55)
nodes.quote: Socratic AI fallacy diagnostics prompted students to identify circular reasoning and strengthen warrant linkages (g=+0.55).

nodes.name: ev-esl-13: Epistemic Stance Diversity & Critical Questioning (g=-0.19)
nodes.quote: Students receiving one-click AI thesis arguments demonstrated shallower evaluative nuance when formulating independent claims (g=-0.19).

nodes.name: ev-esl-14: Disciplinary Academic Phraseology Index (g=+0.46)
nodes.quote: Interactive AI concordance exploration expanded academic phraseology without inducing formulaic boilerplate prose (g=+0.46).

nodes.name: ev-esl-15: Solo Multi-Source Synthesis Score (g=-0.22)
nodes.quote: Replacing student drafting with AI synthesis resulted in lower conceptual synthesis ability during post-intervention unassisted exams (g=-0.22).

nodes.name: ev-esl-16: Writing Agency & Metacognitive Stance Control (g=+0.47)
nodes.quote: Scaffolding that guided students via Socratic questioning rather than direct edits fostered higher agency and distinct voice (g=+0.47).

nodes.name: CLM-001: Socratic outline scaffol...
nodes.value: Socratic outline scaffolding and argument gap diagnostics significantly improve argumentative essay coherence and claim-evidence alignment.
nodes.quote: Low risk of bias; effects reflect structured drafting support and move-level guidance in formative writing.

nodes.name: CLM-002: Contextual lexical synon...
nodes.value: Contextual lexical synonym suggestions and collocation diagnostics enhance academic register and vocabulary richness.
nodes.quote: Low risk of bias; improvements in academic word density and collocation sophistication are robust across RCTs.

nodes.name: CLM-003: Unguarded reliance on ge...
nodes.value: Unguarded reliance on generative text replacement degrades unassisted critical reasoning, solo argument retention, and authorial voice.
nodes.quote: High risk of scaffolding dependency and voice atrophy if text replacement is unconstrained; mitigated only by mandatory metacognitive critique logs.

nodes.name: ⚠️ Scaffolding Dependency Trap
nodes.value: Cognitive offloading to AI paragraph generation weakens unassisted solo argumentative reasoning.
nodes.quote: Enforce 4-phase fading scaffolding, mandatory reflection logs, and unassisted solo exams.

nodes.name: ⚠️ Authorial Voice Homogenization
nodes.value: Unconstrained sentence rewriting suppresses distinctive non-native rhetoric and stylistic agency.
nodes.quote: Mandate metacognitive justification logs before adopting any AI suggestion.

nodes.name: 🔬 Measurement/Retention Gap
nodes.value: Lack of multi-semester tracking to assess long-term transfer to postgraduate thesis writing.
nodes.quote: Multi-year quasi-experimental cohort tracking in subsequent academic courses.

nodes.name: ⚖️ PILOT
nodes.value: Empirical evidence reveals an acute Task vs. Learning divergence in L2 writing: unguarded AI generation produces immediate drafting fluency (+0.54g) but impairs delayed unassisted critical thinking (-0.23g) and authorial voice (-0.20g). A total ban is educationally unviable, while unconstrained rollout causes severe skill atrophy. Therefore, the tribunal adjudicates a restricted PILOT verdict governed by a 4-phase fading scaffolding protocol and mandatory justification logs.
nodes.quote: Applicable to undergraduate ESL/EAP academic writing compulsory courses; strictly prohibited in unassisted closed-book examinations and high-stakes summative certifications without cognitive guardrails.
